discovery: Cooling, trapping and quantum control of molecules at ultracold temperatures

nominees.name: David DeMille
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Molecules, with their rich internal structure and long-range dipolar interactions, long resisted the methods that made ultracold atoms so powerful. The nominees overcame this. Doyle introduced cryogenic buffer-gas cooling and beams, a general source of cold molecules, and later realized optical tweezer arrays of laser-cooled molecules. DeMille showed that diatomic molecules can be laser cooled despite vibrational branching (SrF, 2010) and captured them in a magneto-optical trap, while also pioneering molecular precision tests of fundamental symmetries. Ye produced the first near-degenerate gas of ground-state polar molecules and demonstrated dipolar quantum many-body physics, ultracold chemistry and molecular quantum control. Together these advances turned molecules into fully controllable quantum systems, now used for quantum simulation, quantum information, searches for the electron electric dipole moment and new physics, and state-resolved chemistry at the quantum limit, a new field spanning physics and chemistry.
